test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A dealer offers a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20%. If the marked price is ₹1,200, then the cost price is:
solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,200

Discount = 10%

Profit = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price × (1 - Discount %)

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price / (1 + Profit %)

**Calculation:**

Discounted Price = ₹1,200 × (1 - 0.10)

⇒ Discounted Price = ₹1,200 × 0.90

⇒ Discounted Price = ₹1,080

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,080

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,080 / (1 + 0.20)

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,080 / 1.20

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = ₹900

**The cost price is ₹900.**
